Meta: The world's first AI-oriented organization?
Mark Shmulik
+1 917 344 8508 mark.shmulik@bernsteinsg.com
Wenhuan Chang
+1 917 344 8546
wenhuan.chang@bernsteinsg.com
Deeksha Pandey
+1 917 344 8447
deeksha.pandey@bernsteinsg.com
AI-anxiety is so widespread that we’re simultaneously looking for, extrapolating, and dismissing ‘how will we work’ proof-points. A sci-fi memo stokes fear, then a barrage of rebuttals. Block slashing nearly half of their workforce could be AI, but could just be Dorsey being Dorsey. Anthropic’s one-person growth marketing team could point to a hyper-lean future, but an enterprise AI-native company is hard to extrapolate. Meta reportedly looking to cut 20% of the workforce could be trimming COVID-related bloat, but Meta has already leaned out. Given Mr. Zuckerberg’s track record, a pivot to an AI-centric org. is worth paying attention to.
AI-washing? Possible but unlikely. Is AI a convenient scapegoat for cuts that might have happened anyway? Perhaps. We’d pivot the framing slightly as layoffs that may have been perceived as a negative signal in a stable period, could now be viewed as support that a company’s seeing tangible AI efficiency gains. But we believe the market will quickly see through companies using AI as camouflage - fat exists in every organization, but it’s usually not as clean as being concentrated in specific teams or individuals. The risk of cutting into muscle for an AI-related press bump seems a bit too short-term to be viewed as good strategy, even if it feels there’s cover on paper.
Two paths to a durable “AI winner.” The first path is well understood. You can build a world-class frontier model and product ecosystem that unlocks entirely new adjacent TAMs. Given management’s request for investor patience on this front, and reports of delays around Avocado, Meta may still come out an AI winner given their talent bench and distribution advantage, but still requires a leap of faith at this point.
The second path is to deploy AI deeply across your core business so that your competitive moat to peers widens beyond dispute. Meta has already demonstrated the compelling returns they’re seeing from deploying AI to core workloads. But if the company can now re-design their operations from the ground up to be AI-forward, their potential cost and performance advantage could be insurmountable.
Meta’s probably the best placed incumbent to pivot to an AI-enabled org of the future. Recall the speed at which the company did a 180 post pandemic and returned to their engineering roots by trimming non-technical roles and ‘flattening’ management layers. Meta has the muscle memory, the internal proof points, and a leader that has seen success in the last big re-org - why wouldn’t they be at the forefront to rebuild the company from the ground up to be ‘AI proof’?
What does an AI-powered Meta organization look like? The company has been quite aggressive at getting their employees to embrace AI by including AI-related adoption metrics in their OKRs, pursuing new AI related productivity initiatives, and re-thinking what’s possible with small teams. Recall Zuckerberg’s comments that “we're starting to see projects that used to require big teams now be accomplished by a single very talented person”.

50:1? Reports hint of a stretch target to flatten the org further to 50:1 employee:manager ratios - well beyond the 7-15:1 ratios that is considered the standard range today. Even at a 20% reduction in headcount, Meta could realize \$2-4B in costsavings this year and \$5-8B in 2027, potentially worth 3-5% EPS upside in 2026 and 4-7% in 2027. But of course these outcomes assume the company pockets the savings, whereas it’s far more likely we see most of the savings redeployed into AIrelated investment.
So which is it, bloat or AI pivot? We think it's mostly the latter, and that raises the real question: what does an AI-enabled org of the future actually look like? It forces a rethink of which functions can be streamlined, which new AI-native teams need to be built, and how companies should measure progress with entirely new KPIs. The conversation goes a lot beyond just cutting headcount...it’s about redesigning the operating model around where AI creates leverage and where human input still drives unique value.
And what does this all mean for the rest of the industry...and society at large? Hard to say, but there could be a wave of panic as everyone scrambles to mirror the archetype Meta appears to be racing for. If one major player is able to redraw the blueprint for an AI-enabled organization, others will rush to replicate it...and we wonder if this could trigger a cascade of hurried pivots, half-formed strategies, and reactive restructuring across the ecosystem.

Amazon.Com Inc

Meta Platforms Inc.
We value Meta on a Price Target of \$900 using a 50/50 combination of 2027e EV/Sales multiple of 8x, and a DCF using a WACC of 10% and a terminal growth of 3.5%. We consider Meta primarily a digital advertising business and benchmark valuation to comparable peers in this industry set.
Reddit Inc

Alphabet Inc
Upside risk to our price target:
• Faster than expected revenue growth tied to digital advertising recovery and idiosyncratic efforts or better than expected margins tied to recent effort to slow down hiring and small scale lay-offs.
• Favorable regulatory outcomes further entrenching Google’s incumbency positions across both Search and Network.
Downside risk to our price target:
Terminal risk narratives tied to Search disintermediation, either from negative headlines or share loss (users and/or revenue) in search. If search were to suffer topline changes it could have a trickle effect across the business and have a material impact on GOOGL's ad revenues and we would expect further de-rating in the stock.
• Alphabet is currently under investigation in multiple regulatory proceedings across both anti-trust and privacy, domestically and abroad. In particular, the DOJ case against Google on Search will likely reach a verdict later this year.
Amazon.Com Inc
Downside risks to our price target:
• Amazon is currently under investigation in multiple regulatory proceedings across both anti-trust and privacy, domestically and abroad. Any regulations or actions by either the FTC, DOJ, or EU agencies could negatively impact the company's financials and valuation.
• New investments such as Groceries, Healthcare, AI, and Other Bets could result in a new investment cycle resulting in elevated capital intensity, compressing operating margins, and lower FCF.
• Share loss across core businesses from new eCommerce entrants and main AWS competitors could derate the multiples associated with both core businesses
Meta Platforms Inc.
Downside risk to our target price:
• Meta is currently under investigation in multiple regulatory proceedings now mostly focused on anti-trust domestically and abroad.
• Signs that we’re reaching maturity in digital ads, increased competition as alternatives emerge with compelling ad ROIs, or further privacy related changes (e.g., Cookie depreciation) could all put press on Meta's revenue outlook resulting in compressing revenue growth and de-rating.
• Meta's metaverse aspirations could lead to margin headwinds and potentially minimal ROIC, which could negatively affect both estimates and multiples.
Reddit Inc
Upside risk to our price target:
• Faster than expected revenue growth helped by more data licensing deals.
• Higher than expected revenue growth if Reddit figures out the new ad platform and monetization accelerate ahead of our timetable.
• Faster than expected margin expansion tied to revenue growth acceleration and moderate expense growth.
Downside risk to our price target:
• Continued volatility in user growth number, particularly in the domestic market
• Data licensing revenue could start to slow and decline down the line
• More than expected revenue impact from macro slow down

Pinterest Inc
Downside risks to our price target:
• With any negative macro events that could put ad budgets under pressure, Pinterest could be at risk of ad dollars moving off the platform and being re-allocated to larger peers with more established direct response products.
• Pinterest trades at a higher multiple to peers with a compelling investor narrative, but if the company is unable to execute successfully on the vision of shifting user behavior towards shopping, recent investor optimism may cool.
• Slower roll out in any of their new products could lead to slower than anticipated revenue growth
Snap Inc
Upside risk to the price target:
• Snap trades heavily around revenue beats and misses, if core advertisers come back and/or the company is able to attract new ad buyers to the improved ad platform, monetization may accelerate ahead of our timetable.
• Snap’s current investor narrative is unclear at the moment with limited investor confidence in management’s forward looking commentary, efforts to improve investor messaging alongside proof of progress (potentially new partnership announcements) could win back investors and re-rate the stock.
Downside risk to the price target:
• With any negative macro events that could put ad budgets under pressure, Snapchat could be at risk of ad dollars moving off the platform and being re-allocated to larger peers with more established direct response products. If Snapchat is also unable to overcome ad measuring and tracking issues successfully, they could lose advertisers.
• Snapchat's primary users are Gen Z and younger millennials – a notoriously finicky group. Newer entrants like TikTok, Roblox, and several in-development apps are also going after this same age demo which could result in SNAP losing their status as the social home of this demo, which would severely dampen the financials and valuation of the company.
